name: Bethnal Green Market
summary: A street market on Bethnal Green Road, E2, selling a range of goods from clothing to fruit and vegetables. Tower Hamlets Council describes the area as a major local shopping area and a social meeting place.

evidence.quote: sells a wide range of items from clothes to fruit and vegetables
Bethnal Green is perhaps better known for its on-going association with boxing, but it is also a major local shopping area and an important social meeting place for the community
almost the whole of one side of Bethnal Green Rd is an open market
attempts have been made to do away with Sunday markets and the street market, always without success
Baroness Burdett Coutts, a wealthy and public spirited lady who, at a cost of £200,000, cleared a large tract of slums
Running every Saturday until 20th December, from 10am–4pm, the market will feature six stalls

story.then: A memoir published in 2017 describes the road's stalls lining nearly one side of the street, with repeated attempts to end the street and Sunday markets failing. In late 2025 a Saturday market with six stalls was scheduled outside E. Pellicci's, running until 20 December.
story.now: The council lists the market as trading Monday to Saturday, 8am to 6pm, on Bethnal Green Road.
worth_knowing: The 2025 pop-up stalls stood outside E. Pellicci Café, which the council calls historic.

story_research.note: No opening date, vibe or website found. Tower Hamlets Slice was refused. Try Historic England, local history societies, the EETG, and Londonist for market origins and the current stalls.
